label: original-phase step ~5 after e/3 preceded by m/3, in sequences starting k/s/n (sparse conjunction)
explanation: Very sparse feature (72 activations). Fires almost only in the original phase (91% of mass), mainly at t=4-6 (64% at t=5), with weak, nearly uniform magnitude (0.10-0.16). Typical context: first token k/s/n, the previous token e or 3, two back m/3/x, as in k s 3 m 3 [e][h] or s n r m e [e]. Current input leans toward e/u/h/r. It never fires on the delimiter and rarely in the copy phase (3 steps, outputs at recall_idx 2-4). Yet many sequences match this context and stay silent, so the predicate has about 1.5% precision even at 73% recall. Adding a current-token whitelist only reaches about 5-11% precision. The feature looks like a specific hidden-state configuration (a conjunction of earlier tokens) that these variables do not capture compactly. No magnitude structure was found.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 22 cues. Raise it: orig0=k (+2.29), prev_tok=e (+2.12), in_tok=u (+1.92), orig0=s (+1.77), prev2_tok=m (+1.57), prev2_tok=3 (+1.49). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-1.65), orig_idx=-1 (-1.63).
